1.3.title: Objection 3: uncertainty calibration
1.3.status: Status: on hold pending the lead author's decision on the recommendation to drop resampling blocks of raw weeks. The reason comes from the application. Even in a quiet period under the gamma-frailty model, the expected death rate changes with baseline risk and with who is still alive. Moving a block to a different point in follow-up mixes death rates from different times and alters the trajectory used to fit frailty. Correct survivor counts within the resample still leave the rates at the wrong times. Person resampling keeps death weeks in place and rebuilds counts and risk sets. The [block placement check](objection3_paper_method/block_bootstrap_operationalization/WHY_BLOCK_PLACEMENT_MATTERS.md) illustrates the problem even when the starting counts match the model exactly.

5.11.status: Status: the two approved numerical corrections are implemented in m116; m115 is preserved. Finite weekly death fractions below one use the exact log survival transformation. A fraction of one or outside the valid range raises a warning. The gamma inverse uses the fitted variance independently at each time and evaluates large positive exponents in log space when needed. Unrepresentable results are unavailable rather than clipped. Normalization preserves the valid prefix, including nonlinear correction on that prefix, and logs the first unavailable week per cohort.
